auditReviewer.type: independent-first-stage content audit followed by comparison

corrections.reason: Canonical includes corresponding grid points but does not explicitly require drawing all symmetry lines; native fold-line identification and drawing are not fully represented.
Native parent includes recursive processes and combining standard function types via its children. Canonical contextual explicit formulas/domain analysis do not cover that full scope.

Native children include graph/table inverse values and restricting a noninvertible function to make it invertible. Canonical affine inverses/composition and bijection checks do not explicitly cover these tasks.
Canonical set-to-set unique correspondence/domain/range covers the definition, but native also requires f(x) notation and graph as equation y=f(x).
Canonical algebraic/domain and contextual restrictions omit relating domain to the graph. Native graph-domain interpretation does not require radical/denominator restriction procedures.
Average-rate quotient/secant slope matches, but table interpretation and graph estimation in native are not explicit canonical tasks; the complete standard is not exact.

Canonical chooses linear/quadratic/exponential models and evaluates them; native parent includes proving equal differences versus factors and classifying constant absolute/percent rates. Neither full scope includes the other.
Canonical adds coordinate area calculations; native includes coordinate polygon drawing and contextual problems. Coordinate-area capability alone is not equivalent to this native standard.
Signed opposite quantities match, but native explicitly requires explaining what zero means in each context; canonical does not include that criterion.
Canonical adds polygon areas, while native requires all-quadrant contextual plotting and explicitly absolute-value distance use. Exact scope is overstated.
Canonical emphasizes quotient/value of a ratio; native emphasizes ratio language for relationships between quantities. These overlap but have distinct requirements.
Canonical covers strict/weak half-planes and intersections and additionally requires redundant-constraint and bounded-polygon-boundary analysis.
Canonical includes the full linear-divisor remainder/factor theorem plus general polynomial division and constraining a general remainder.

Canonical recognizes proportional functions, finds k and graphs them; native requires constructing a proportional equation from quantities/context. Construction is not guaranteed by recognizing/graphing a supplied formula.
Canonical probability range/certain/impossible classifications omit native probability near 0, 1/2, 1 and relative likelihood interpretation.
Canonical outcome-count computation/meaning overlaps uniform probability, but does not explicitly require developing the model and assigning probabilities to each outcome.

Canonical finite equally likely classical probability with combination counting overlaps the compound-event fraction interpretation; compound-event reasoning and general sample-space modeling are not explicitly equivalent.

Transposition and combining in ax+b=cx+d do not explicitly include distributive expansion; native requires rational-coefficient equations including distribution. Do not borrow distribution from another node.
Parenthesized-equation expansion is a component; canonical does not alone explicitly establish the whole rational-coefficient linear-equation scope required natively.

Canonical relates intersections of two linear-function graphs to systems, which does not cover native systems containing a vertical line. Avoid equating all linear-equation systems with two function graphs.
Canonical gives unique dependent values but omits native graph-as-set-of-ordered-input/output-pairs requirement.
Canonical square-root bracketing/comparison is a restricted component of native arbitrary irrational rational approximation, finer approximation and approximate number-line placement.
Canonical definitions and angle-only dependence omit the native similarity-based justification of invariance of right-triangle ratios.
Canonical theorem application/multiplicity tasks do not require showing the theorem for quadratic polynomials. Native quadratic verification is material, not supplied by knowing the general theorem.

Canonical rounds to a required precision and counts significant digits; native requires choosing appropriate accuracy from measurement limitations. Executing specified rounding is not the whole decision task.

Canonical states the product criterion and computes probabilities assuming independence; native explicitly applies it to decide whether events are independent. Distinguishing independence from disjointness is additional canonical content.
Canonical conditional multiplication applies to general event probability models with nonzero-condition handling; native restricts application to a uniform model.
Native parent includes fitting functions and analyzing residuals through its children; canonical drawing scatterplots and judging correlation sign is a restricted component.
Canonical distinguishes additive from multiplicative change and predicts from either model. Native child asks only to recognize constant additive rate.
Canonical fixed-ratio discrete sequences include calculating future terms; native recognizes constant percent rates per interval without restricting quantities to a discrete sequence.
Canonical verifies inverse compositions and additionally checks bijection/domain facts and finds affine inverses.
Canonical numeric comparison adds approximate differences but omits explicitly recording >, = and <; native asks both comparison and symbolic recording.
Canonical addition commutativity/associativity does not explicitly cover native subtraction strategies as well.
Canonical inverse relations cover unknown addends and factors, but do not alone explicitly cover all three-number addition/subtraction equations, including an unknown minuend/subtrahend/result.
Native expanded form is not explicit in canonical reading/writing/numeral-place meanings; a larger numerical bound does not fill that omission.
Canonical composition by place value does not alone include native reading/writing number names as well as numerals and expanded form.
Canonical compares and orders with a larger number bound, but native explicitly requires recording >, = and <, not specified canonically.
Canonical unknown-factor inverse relation is not the full set of unknown multiplication/division equations, including unknown dividends/divisors/results.
Native parent children require unit-fraction multiple interpretation, visual models and word problems. Canonical fraction-times-integer algorithm alone omits these material tasks.
Fraction-equivalence transformation is one component; native also adds fractions with denominators 10 and 100. Equivalence alone does not contain the full standard.
Identifying power notation and sign distinctions is not writing and evaluating arbitrary numerical expressions with whole-number exponents.
Evaluating individual powers is only a component of numerical-expression writing/evaluation with exponents; negative-base sign rules add different canonical scope.
Mixed numerical evaluation covers much native calculation but does not explicitly require writing exponent expressions; order-of-operations scope also adds material.
Mixed numerical arithmetic contains no variable substitution or formula evaluation, which are essential native tasks. Cannot inherit them from cnm_029.
Canonical solves supplied equations but native also requires writing equations from real-world problems; p146 supplies that separate component.
Inequality definitions/solution sets omit native number-line representation and infinite-solution recognition.
Number-line representation alone omits constructing inequalities from contextual constraints; closed endpoints add canonical scope.
Contextual inequality modeling with integer/optimal solutions does not explicitly include graphing full solution sets and recognizing infinite solutions.
Canonical GCF with unrestricted bounds omits native LCM and distributive rewriting. A larger number range cannot make an individual component contain a compound standard.
Canonical LCM with unrestricted bounds omits native GCF and distributive rewriting. A larger number range cannot make an individual component contain a compound standard.
Native requires contextual modeling and comparison of algebraic and arithmetic solution sequences; canonical transposition/combination alone does not include them.
Canonical parenthesized-equation solution omits native contextual modeling and comparing algebraic versus arithmetic solution sequences.
Canonical linear modeling does not require native comparing algebraic and arithmetic solution sequences; it also includes additional linear equation forms.
Solving and graphing supplied linear inequalities omits native creating the inequality from a word problem and interpreting its solution in context.
Contextual inequality modeling lacks explicit graphing of the solution set; it adds integer optimization beyond native specified forms.
Graphing a given inequality solution set is one component and omits native constructing, solving and interpreting contextual inequalities.

Canonical optimization by functions/inequalities/geometry does not encompass every geometric design problem, such as satisfying nonoptimization physical constraints or typographic grids. Its algebraic optimization also extends beyond native geometry.
Conic hyperbola x^2/a^2-y^2/b^2=1 and its two oblique asymptotes do not represent a single rational function graph y=r(x). Sharing the word hyperbola/asymptote is insufficient semantic alignment.

Canonical constant-step sequence continuation includes arbitrary/noninteger sequences and does not require arithmetic-table/property explanations; native pattern justification is not represented. Neither scope contains the other.

Canonical includes calculator evaluation at general angles, outside native specified special-angle and unit-circle identities; native geometric derivation is omitted, so narrower containment is overstated.

Canonical reduction formulas include pi/2 +/- alpha, outside native requested transformed angles; canonical criteria cover only sine/cosine, while native also tangent and 2pi-x. Neither full scope contains the other.
Canonical numerical reduction examples and restricted result criteria differ from native arbitrary-real-angle identities and special-triangle derivations; no subset relationship is established.
Canonical choosing mean/median/mode includes mode, outside the listed native center measures; native distribution-shape-based group center/spread comparison is not all captured.
Canonical range and variance calculations exceed native listed IQR/SD spread summaries and omit shape-based center/measure selection, so narrower is not established.
Computing the quartiles includes more than IQR comparison while native requires distribution-shape-based measure selection and centers. Keep overlap without asserting full containment.
Canonical variance comparison/decisions under equal or similar means adds a variance-specific condition and does not include native shape-based measure selection. Partial is the justified relation.
Canonical boxplot construction/reading includes extrema and five-number summaries beyond native listed center/spread comparison. Native choice by distribution shape is missing.
Omitted close match: primary letters node explicitly represents variable numbers and quantity relations by expressions. It additionally includes operation laws, so partial is safer than exact.
Omitted concept component: percent meaning as a ratio with denominator 100 is directly required by native percent-as-rate-per-100 language. This alone does not cover either numerical application.
Add partial cnm_055: comparing segment lengths by measurement/superposition overlaps comparing lengths, but ordering three/indirect third-object comparison are missing.
Add partial cnm_p167: equal-value fractions are explicit canonical content, though canonical multiplication/division transformation differs from native equal-size/number-line equivalence meaning.

Add partial cnm_055: segment-length comparison by measurement or superposition directly overlaps the length case; native includes object attributes such as weight and verbal difference interpretation.
Add partial cnm_h098 and cnm_h101: geometric modulus and complex differences are actual components of complex distance, but general difference-distance and midpoint computation remain incomplete.
Add partial cnm_h098 and cnm_h101: geometric modulus and complex differences are actual components of complex distance, but general difference-distance and midpoint computation remain incomplete.
Add partial cnm_h133: comparing means from two sample groups directly overlaps treatment comparison, but randomized experiment design and simulation significance are missing.
